name: Otago Polytechnic
summary: Dunedin polytechnic with an Auckland campus, teaching 17 hands-on bachelor's degrees to international students, from nursing and design to IT.

ib.text: Degree level lists completion of the IB Diploma with 24 points or more; IELTS Academic 6.0 with no band under 5.5 applies if English is not your first language. Some degrees add a portfolio or statement.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Veterinary Nursing
programmes.about: A three-year degree combining veterinary nursing knowledge and clinical skills with extensive workplace experience; years 1 and 2 are on campus and year 3 is online with a work placement.
programmes.selectionNote: The page asks for University Entrance or equivalent and sets no ranking; year 3 can start in February or July.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Architectural Studies (Architectural Technology) or (Interior Architecture)
programmes.about: Builds skills in drawing, computer-aided design, building science, construction and communication, leading to work as an architectural technologist or interior architect, or to further study to become a registered architect.
programmes.ib: Applicants are assessed individually from their IB results; a portfolio is part of selection.
programmes.selectionNote: Selected on your portfolio and academic record; applications are accepted until late November, and earlier ones are processed first.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Construction (Quantity Surveying)
programmes.about: Trains construction professionals to price and manage construction projects, with the technical, work-ready skills for roles in quantity surveying.
programmes.selectionNote: The page sets entry requirements but no ranking is published; Dunedin starts in February or July and Auckland has further intakes.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Applied Management
programmes.about: A business degree built around industry experience, with an internship semester in the third year in which you complete a research project inside a real business.
programmes.selectionNote: The page sets entry requirements but no ranking is published; there are several intakes a year in Dunedin and Auckland.

family.name: Bachelor of Applied Management
family.differs: The general management degree, with a third-year internship semester.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Applied Management (Accounting)
programmes.about: An applied accounting qualification with case studies, applied assignments and a workplace-based industry project, aimed at becoming a chartered accountant or a CPA Australia certified accountant.
programmes.selectionNote: You must be 16 by the start; the page sets entry requirements but no ranking is published.

family.name: Bachelor of Applied Management
family.differs: The accounting version, taught in Dunedin, with an industry project.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Visual Arts
programmes.about: A first year of core art courses, methodology and art history, then one of seven studio disciplines, including ceramics and jewellery, in which to develop your own practice.
programmes.ib: Successful art units and a portfolio are part of entry.
programmes.selectionNote: Entry asks for five years of secondary school with successful art units and a portfolio; July entry is advanced entry only.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Design (Fashion)
programmes.about: A fashion degree built on sustainability, industry connections and hands-on courses, where you develop your own style and identity as a designer.
programmes.selectionNote: The page sets entry requirements but no ranking is published.

family.name: Bachelor of Design
family.differs: Fashion design, with a focus on sustainability.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Design (Communication)
programmes.about: Teaches you to craft ideas and tell stories through still and moving images, text, sound and interactive media, with community and client projects focused on social and environmental change.
programmes.selectionNote: The page sets entry requirements but no ranking is published.

family.name: Bachelor of Design
family.differs: Still and moving image, text, sound and interactive media.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Design (Product)
programmes.about: Teaches you to design products, services and systems with human needs and sustainability at the core, building and testing prototypes to develop conceptualisation and drawing skills.
programmes.selectionNote: The page sets entry requirements but no ranking is published.

family.name: Bachelor of Design
family.differs: Products, services and systems, with prototypes.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Information Technology
programmes.about: A broad first year in IT, then a focus in software development, IT infrastructure, network engineering or alternative digital platforms, with the option of a game development focus and industry projects.
programmes.selectionNote: All eligible applicants are accepted unless applications exceed places; then they are interviewed and ranked by an admissions panel.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Engineering Technology
programmes.about: An Engineering New Zealand accredited degree in civil, mechanical or electrical engineering, building skills in management, economics, communication and problem-solving.
programmes.ib: The entry list names Level 3 Physics and Calculus; ask Otago Polytechnic how IB Physics and Maths count.
programmes.selectionNote: Eligible applicants are chosen by the entry criteria; if applications exceed places, a waiting list runs in order of application.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Culinary Arts
programmes.about: Combines technical cooking skills, creative design tools and food business practice, learned by hands-on experience in the kitchen.
programmes.ib: A CV and a letter of application of up to 500 words are part of entry.
programmes.selectionNote: The admissions committee reads your CV and letter of application; the May intake is for assessment of prior learning only.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Social Services (Specialty)
programmes.about: Prepares you to work as a social services professional in New Zealand, with self-awareness, an understanding of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and the communication skills to support diverse people.
programmes.ib: A written statement of 500 to 700 words is part of entry.
programmes.selectionNote: You write a statement on why you want to work with people in contemporary Aotearoa New Zealand.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Midwifery
programmes.about: A four-year degree leading to registration as a midwife in New Zealand, with theory, real-life midwifery experience, online learning and compulsory block courses in Dunedin or Waikanae.
programmes.ib: The Midwifery Council asks for 18 Level 3 credits in Biology, Chemistry or Physics and an English-rich subject; ask how IB subjects count.
programmes.selectionNote: The page sets University Entrance plus Midwifery Council subject credits; no ranking is published.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Nursing
programmes.about: A degree in nursing practice, human behaviour, pharmacology and body systems, with a simulation suite and practice placements, leading to the State Final Examination.
programmes.ib: Entry names a science, an English-rich subject and one other approved subject; ask how IB subjects count.
programmes.selectionNote: Applications for the 2027 intake have closed and 2028 opens in mid-2027; a selection committee reviews academic records and two referee reports.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Occupational Therapy
programmes.about: Centred on working with people, with five placements for practice experience, leading to registration as an occupational therapist in New Zealand.
programmes.selectionNote: Places go on prior academic success and diversity of life experience; you may be asked to an interview. July entry is part-time and limited.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Applied Science
programmes.about: A degree built on practical experience and problem-based learning in sport, exercise and health, plus communication, academic writing and project management, with community projects.
programmes.selectionNote: If there are more applicants than places, a panel interviews and ranks them with weight on academic record.

notes: Most degrees list a lower first-year international fee with a scholarship applied, by NZ$2,000 to NZ$3,500; the figures here are the standard fees.
Honours degrees and the Infrastructure Asset Management apprenticeship are not listed; the apprenticeship page says it is not available to international students.
Construction, Applied Management and Information Technology can also be taken at the Auckland International campus, with intakes in February, April, July and October 2027.
